text:
Mika Zibanejad has 15 points in 18 games, and 12 of them are assists. For a center who scored 34 goals last season, three goals stand out, and it isn't only bad luck. His individual expected goals, the quality of his own chances, have fallen to 0.68 per 60 minutes from 1.02 last season. He has one goal in his last 10.

Some of it is finishing. He's shooting 9.4% against a typical range around 14%, and New York has scored 4.28 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. The bigger worry is volume: 32 shots in 18 games from a player whose shot still ranks in the 97th percentile for speed on NHL EDGE.

The good news is in the team numbers. With him at five-on-five, the Rangers get almost 54% of the expected goals, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving his own zone with possession on 71% of his exits last season. Our range still projects 25 goals over the full season (18 to 33). At 33, we'd want to see whether the shots come back before writing off the goals.
headline: Zibanejad is setting up, but the shot has gone quiet
